subject: Medicaid work requirements
query: when do medicaid work requirements start
title: When do Medicaid work requirements start? Jan. 1, 2027, in most states
answer: Under the 2025 federal budget law, states must begin Medicaid work requirements for adults in the Affordable Care Act expansion group by Jan. 1, 2027. A few states are earlier: Nebraska started May 1, 2026, Montana planned July 1, 2026, and Iowa plans Dec. 1, 2026. States showing a good-faith effort can get more time, until Dec. 31, 2028, at the latest.
body:
The rule covers expansion adults through age 64. To keep coverage, they must log 80 hours a month of work, community service or a work program, or qualify for an exemption, according to KFF. Mandatory exemptions include parents and caretakers of children 13 and under, people who are medically frail, and people who are pregnant or postpartum. States may also grant short-term hardship exceptions.

States check compliance when someone applies, looking back at least one month and up to three months, and again at renewal, which for this group happens every six months. Arkansas began a "soft" launch on July 1, 2026, with no one losing coverage before Jan. 1, 2027. Georgia, the only state with an operating work-requirement waiver, has a waiver that expires Dec. 31, 2026.

The Congressional Budget Office projected $326 billion in federal Medicaid savings over 10 years, mainly from people losing coverage.
in_the_news: With less than two months left before the Jan. 1, 2027, federal deadline, states are preparing to enforce the new Medicaid work rules, and Iowa plans to start Dec. 1, 2026.

faq.q: What is the start date for Medicaid work requirements?
faq.a: Jan. 1, 2027, is the federal deadline. Some states started earlier, and others may get extensions up to Dec. 31, 2028.

faq.q: How many hours do you have to work to keep Medicaid?
faq.a: 80 hours a month of work, community service, a work program or a combination, unless you are exempt.

faq.q: Who is exempt from Medicaid work requirements?
faq.a: Mandatory exemptions include parents and caretakers of children 13 and under, people who are medically frail, and people who are pregnant or postpartum, among others.

faq.q: Do Medicaid work requirements apply to everyone on Medicaid?
faq.a: No. They apply to adults covered through the ACA Medicaid expansion, through age 64.

faq.q: Which states started Medicaid work requirements early?
faq.a: Nebraska (May 1, 2026), Montana (planned July 1, 2026) and Iowa (planned Dec. 1, 2026). Arkansas began a soft launch on July 1, 2026.
